title: Acme support assistant v2: the stack
subtitle: The tools for the routed workflow, an Azure variant against an open-weight variant, with every price taken from an example table.

verdict.text: **Use variant A, Azure.** It is the only variant the brief clears for customers, because the brief accepts a local model for internal tools only. It comes to USD EXAMPLE 1,171.01 a month against the €1,500 budget, so it appears to fit, but those prices are made up, and the dollars are compared with the euros with no rate applied. The how-to path takes 4.95 s [guess] against 5 s, which leaves almost no margin until a real call is measured.

sections.title: Constraints
sections.intro: These come from the brief and the pattern page, and they remove candidates before any price is read.

blocks.text: **Every price on this page is EXAMPLE.** Token prices come from the example table, which is made up. That table has no rows for services, so the search, hosting, database, tracing and GPU lines are placeholders made up for this page. No provider page was read and nothing was looked up online. Replace all of them before quoting any figure.

items: **Customer data stays in the EU** (brief, Rules). Removes the public API endpoint the prototype defaults to, and any model deployment that may process outside the EU, such as a global deployment type [med].
**Acme already has an Azure tenant in West Europe** (brief). Everything defaults to it, and anything new has to earn its place.
**No GPU servers on-prem** (brief, Rules). Removes a model on Acme's own hardware. A local or open model would have to run on a rented GPU server in the tenant.

**A local model is acceptable for internal tools** (brief, Rules). This assistant answers customers, so the brief does not clear a local model for it, and the pattern page reads it the same way. Removes a local model as the recommended choice. Variant B is costed for comparison only and needs Acme's written agreement before it could be used.
**The model holds no tools and code sends every reply** (pattern page). Removes any need for tool calling or an agent framework.
**First visible words within 5 seconds at p95 in chat** (brief, as the pattern page reads it). Removes a second model call before the answer shows, and any check that waits for the whole answer.
**About €1,500 a month for models and hosting together**, at 3,000 questions a day (brief).

**Serbian in Latin and Cyrillic and English, retrieval across languages, exact match on codes such as E3 and SKUs** (pattern page, Documents). Removes vector-only search, which is what the prototype does.
**Who runs it after hand-over is not stated** [guess]. The brief names 6 support agents and no IT or operations team, which weighs against anything self-managed.

blocks.text: **The how-to path has almost no margin.** At the pattern page's guess of 2 seconds per model call it takes 4.95 s. At 2.5 seconds per call it takes 5.95 s and misses the target. A small router that answers in 1 second brings it to 3.95 s, and that is the first fix to try. The output check holds the first sentence until code has passed it, so no unchecked text reaches the customer, and that hold is counted.

items: **Replace every price.** The offer needs the providers' prices for tokens and services, and an exchange rate, each with its date.
**Confirm the model and version in West Europe**, in a deployment type that keeps processing in the EU.
**Measure two model calls in a row from West Europe.** This is the one assumption that can break the pattern, and the how-to path has almost no margin.

**Quotas for the peak.** At 400 questions an hour and the brief's mix: answer 11,733 tokens per minute, route 5,667, claim extraction 848, order extraction 575, query embedding 293. These are computed from guessed token counts and are averages, so ask for headroom above them.
**Data processing terms:** retention, abuse monitoring and any human review of prompts, no training on prompts, and the agreement that covers customer data in the EU.
**Private networking** from Container Apps to the model, search and the database.
**Serbian quality on each candidate model**, in Latin and Cyrillic, on the labelled sets.
**Who operates this after hand-over**, by name.
**The open questions on the pattern page**, above all whether a live stock source exists and whether HelpLine can take tickets by API.
**If Acme wants variant B:** its written agreement, GPU quota in West Europe, a second server or a fallback, and someone to run it.
